t: An Early Postclassic state ruled from Tula in Hidalgo, a city of perhaps 30,000–60,000 people at its height in the 11th century.
Its warrior statues, colonnaded halls and chacmools have close parallels at Chichén Itzá, though the nature of that link is debated.
The Aztecs revered the Toltecs as founders of civilisation; Tula itself was abandoned around 1150, amid a severe drought.
dyk: In Nahuatl the word toltecatl, ‘Toltec’, came to mean a skilled artisan, and the Aztecs called art and refinement toltecayotl, ‘Toltec-ness’.
ev: Monumental building begins at Tula Chico, the first civic centre of Tula
Construction starts at Tula Grande, the new ceremonial centre to the south
The growing city absorbs the populations of Tula Chico and Cerro Magoni
The Late Tollan phase begins; the city covers about 16 square kilometres
A severe drought begins, lasting until about 1167
Tula is largely abandoned and the Toltec state comes to an end
The Palacio Quemado and the ceremonial centre are burned

f.founder: Unknown; legend names Mixcoatl and Ce Acatl Topiltzin Quetzalcoatl
f.predecessor: Tula Chico and other Coyotlatelco-period communities
f.successor: Culhuacan and other city-states of the Basin of Mexico
